daily_thesis: The August 5 batch asks when an agent should trust, refresh, or discard internal state. Quo Vadis broadens world models into feedback proxies, SLAMFormer-infinity removes fixed-distance assumptions from map memory, Continue or Replan turns action horizons into a learned validity decision, and DRIFT attacks the denoising trajectory before the final VLA action. APRL should build a state-validity benchmark that couples map memory, replanning, proprioception, and physical attention attacks.

clusters.cluster: World models become feedback proxies for action decisions
clusters.why: Quo Vadis reframes world models as agent feedback proxies, CrossScope and LiLa-WAM specialize WAMs for surgical or manipulation state, Enfold and EmbodiedVAE compress embodied predictive representations, SUV treats future driving scene understanding as video generation, and ValueFormer adds causal value labels. The shared question is what internal proxy changes the next action.
clusters.confidence_note: World-model papers appear across Generation, Robot Learning, and Driving with explicit action or value links.
clusters.lab_action: Classify each world proxy by feedback type, state variable, action it changes, real rollout metric, and stop condition when proxy and reality diverge.

strategy_board.title: State-validity benchmark for robot agents
strategy_board.thesis: Couple map memory, action chunk age, proprioceptive history, and attack trajectory into one validity benchmark.
strategy_board.one_week: Instrument one VLA rollout with chunk age, replan decision, proprioception window, map age, and denoising-step drift.
strategy_board.four_week: Build a small suite where stale map, stale chunk, missing proprioception, and adversarial patch are crossed.
strategy_board.success: The benchmark predicts failure family before final action failure in at least two stress conditions.
strategy_board.stop: State validity signals do not separate failure families beyond generic confidence.
strategy_board.asset: Robot-agent state-validity logs plus replayable stress scenarios.
